**Explored #887 lane collector — worktree plumbing algorithm, dedup tiebreak, scope**

What: Completed sdd-explore for issue #887 (feat/memory: the lane collector — worktree plumbing, no checkout, deterministic dedup on divergence; #864 task 3.1a). Full exploration written to openspec/changes/issue-887-lane-collector/explore.md (~193 lines) in worktree /home/gandalf/IA/brain-issue-887.

Why: #887 implements the collector half (L4+C2) of the #862 ruling (ADR-0034: brain/project/decisions/adr-0034-memory-travels-on-its-own-lane.md). Scope: produce a LOCAL lane commit/branch ref only via git plumbing — no push, no PR (that's #888).

Where: brain/scripts/memory/lane/plan.mjs (pure planner) + brain/scripts/memory/lane/collect.mjs (IO shell) to be created; cli.mjs (VALID_OPS + backend-agnostic dispatch before line 431); package.json (memory:collect script); i18n/{en,es}.mjs (memory.collect.* keys).

Learned (non-obvious):
- Record store is now ONE FILE PER RECORD (`.memory/records/<YYYY-MM>-rec-<id>.jsonl`, post-#677 split-records) — confirmed live. This means the reader's "earliest month file, earliest physical line" first-wins rule (brain/scripts/memory/lib/duplicates.mjs:20-24, store.mjs#readRecords:349-399) DEGENERATES to "line 1 of both copies" when two worktrees hold the same filename — it cannot discriminate. That's exactly why the design adds a second tiebreak: order candidate copies by lexicographic WORKTREE PATH.
- No existing code in brain/scripts reads `git worktree list --porcelain` as a data source — searched exhaustively, every existing worktree usage is add/remove/prune (ticket-branch.mjs:58-59, cold-boot.mjs:83-93, checkpoint.mjs:281-282). lane/collect.mjs would be the first enumerator.
- Secret-scrub precedent: backends/engram.mjs:394-407 already scans all pending records and THROWS BEFORE ANY APPEND on a hit (memory.share.secretFoundRecords), fail-closed, no bypass flag except governance.memorySecretAllowPatterns. Direct precedent for the collector's scrub-before-collect behavior (open question: skip-one-bad-file vs abort-whole-batch — share() aborts the batch, but collector's unattended-run context argues for skip-and-report).
- Git seam to copy: brain/scripts/governance/postmerge/git-seam.mjs — gitTry (:27, never throws) / gitOrThrow (:54, throws with .status). Distinct from brain/scripts/vcs/lib/exec.mjs's run/setSpawn (that's for gh/glab, not git plumbing) — do not conflate.
- cli.mjs backend-agnostic dispatch pattern: reindex/audit/resolve-index/split-records/migrate-v1 all dispatch BEFORE backend selection (cli.mjs:431) because they're not MEMORY_BACKEND concerns — collect should follow the same pattern, never routing through a backend's share().
- All git plumbing commands in the ADR's algorithm verified live and read-only in this session: `git worktree list --porcelain`, `git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>`, `git hash-object -w --path`, `git update-index --add --cacheinfo <mode>,<oid>,<path>` all confirmed against `git help` and live output in /home/gandalf/IA/brain-issue-887 (82+ real worktrees).
- Open questions flagged for sdd-propose: (1) idempotency on same-day re-run — append commit onto existing lane ref vs new -<n> branch (leaning: append, since -<n> is for cross-host name collision, not same-host re-run); (2) scrub granularity (skip-file vs abort-batch); (3) confirm verb name `collect` doesn't collide with #888's `brain:memory:ship` trigger verb; (4) plan.test.mjs must assert tiebreak stability across repeated runs, not just single-run correctness.
- Tests to write (STRICT TDD): brain/scripts/memory/lane/plan.test.mjs (pure unit), brain/scripts/memory/lane/collect.integration.test.mjs (real temp git repo + two real `git worktree add` scratch trees, pattern from resolve-index.integration.test.mjs:23-90 and bootstrap.worktree.test.mjs:82/cold-boot.mjs:83-93).
